UOC CRIS vs. OpenAlex: Publication Coverage and Metadata Consistency

DOI-based comparison, 2010–2025

Bruna Santanach

15 octubre 2026

1 Executive summary

Key findings (publications 2010–2025, matched by normalised DOI)

  • Scale. CRIS holds 15,497 publications (59.4% with DOI); OpenAlex holds 12,418 UOC-affiliated works (92.9% with DOI).
  • OpenAlex → CRIS. 51.1% of OpenAlex records carrying a DOI are already in CRIS. 5,638 DOIs are missing. Identified causes: (1) 1,474 (26.1%) belong to authors whose ORCID is not in our researcher database, i.e. a likely erroneous UOC affiliation in OpenAlex (72.4% of them are Article; 75.4% were published in 2018 or later (median year 2021)); (2) datasets and “Other” types: 1,547 records (27.4% of missing DOIs): Dataset (979), Other (568); main sources: Harvard Dataverse (871), Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) (101), SSRN Electronic Journal (88); (3) non-academic opinion and outreach journals: 747 records (13.2% of missing DOIs): COMeIN (547), Mosaic (200).
  • CRIS → OpenAlex. 63.9% of CRIS DOIs are found as UOC-affiliated OpenAlex works, 31.7% exist in OpenAlex without UOC affiliation, and 4.4% are not found at all.
  • Open-access bias. Records whose DOI is missing from CRIS have an OA share of 76.6% versus 57.3% for matched records (difference +19.3 pp; chi-squared p <1e-04, statistically significant). Using all OpenAlex-UOC records instead of CRIS-confirmed ones shifts the institutional OA rate by +8.7 pp.
  • CRIS DOIs not found in OpenAlex. Of the CRIS DOIs not matched to UOC works, 87.9% exist in OpenAlex without UOC affiliation and 12.1% are absent. Among the 401 absent records, the main typology is Dataset (67.3%) and the main editor/publisher is Repositori de dades de recerca (36.4%).
  • Metadata. Across 5,881 shared DOIs: document type agrees in 91.2% of cases, publication year in 82.3% (exact), and open-access status in 78.2%.

2 Scope and method

  • Sources. CRIS: VW_DIM_PUBLICACIONS_UOC_PLANA_2010 (Snowflake). OpenAlex: works_UOC (UOC-affiliated works, enriched with ORCID / author-in-system flags, dissertations excluded).
  • Matching key. DOIs are normalised identically in both systems (prefix https://doi.org/ removed, trimmed, lower-cased). Records without DOI cannot be matched and are reported separately as No DOI.
  • Typologies. CRIS and OpenAlex types are mapped to a common vocabulary (see type_map_cris / type_map_openalex).
  • Status labels.
Perspective Label Meaning
OpenAlex record Found in CRIS DOI exists in CRIS
Not in CRIS DOI absent from CRIS (further split by cause)
CRIS record Found in OpenAlex (UOC) DOI present in works_UOC
In OpenAlex, not UOC-affiliated DOI exists in OpenAlex but not attributed to UOC
Not in OpenAlex DOI not found in OpenAlex at all

Match indicators. Four percentages are reported per typology, always with the source system’s own records as denominator: OpenAlex found in CRIS and CRIS found in OpenAlex, each expressed (i) over all publications of the source system and (ii) over its publications with a DOI. Only records with a DOI can be matched, so (ii) is the like-for-like coverage measure.

4 OpenAlex DOIs not tracked in CRIS

4.1 Overall status and ORCID context

Each OpenAlex record is classified by whether its DOI exists in CRIS and by the ORCID status of its UOC author(s):

  • ORCID in system – UOC author with ORCID recognised in CRIS.
  • ORCID not in system – OpenAlex attributes UOC affiliation to an author with an ORCID that is not in our researcher database.
  • Author in system / no ORCID and No UOC author in OpenAlex – remaining cases.
DOI status in CRIS by ORCID status of the UOC author
ORCID status Found in CRIS Not in CRIS No DOI
Author in system / no ORCID 26 (66.7%) 13 (33.3%) 0 (0.0%)
No UOC author in OpenAlex 303 (15.9%) 1,282 (67.3%) 320 (16.8%)
ORCID in system 5,471 (62.4%) 2,869 (32.7%) 429 (4.9%)
ORCID not in system 100 (5.9%) 1,474 (86.5%) 131 (7.7%)

4.2 Explaining the gap

OpenAlex records with a DOI absent from CRIS, by identified cause
Cause Records % of missing DOIs
  1. Erroneous UOC affiliation (ORCID not in CRIS)
1,474 26.1%
  1. Dataset / other typology (outside CRIS scope)
1,547 27.4%
  1. Non-academic opinion / outreach journal
747 13.2%
Unexplained (to be investigated) 1,870 33.2%

26.1% of the DOIs missing from CRIS (1,474 records) belong to authors OpenAlex affiliates with UOC but whose ORCID is not in our researcher database. Two further causes are classified in the table above. Erroneous affiliation: 72.4% of them are Article; 75.4% were published in 2018 or later (median year 2021). Datasets and “Other” types: 1,547 records (27.4% of missing DOIs): Dataset (979), Other (568); main sources: Harvard Dataverse (871), Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) (101), SSRN Electronic Journal (88). Non-academic opinion and outreach journals (sources listed in outreach_sources_regex, defined by manual review): 747 records (13.2% of missing DOIs): COMeIN (547), Mosaic (200). Records matching none of them remain unexplained (see Next steps).

6 Does mis-assignment bias open-access figures?

Question. If OpenAlex wrongly attributes publications to UOC, is the apparent open-access (OA) rate overestimated? We compare OA status between OpenAlex records whose DOI is confirmed in CRIS and those that are not.

6.1 OA share by CRIS match

Open-access share by DOI match with CRIS (records with DOI)
Group Records OA records % OA
DOI in CRIS 5,900 3,379 57.3%
DOI not in CRIS 5,638 4,317 76.6%
Statistical tests
Test Result
Chi-squared, OA vs. match group X² = 482.6, p <1e-04
Effect size (phi) 0.205
Two-proportion test, 95% CI of difference (pp) [-21.0, -17.6]
Chi-squared (Monte Carlo), OA status vs. match group p <1e-04

6.2 Adjusted effect (logistic regression)

The association is re-estimated controlling for publication year and typology, to rule out composition effects.

Adjusted odds ratio of being OA for DOIs not in CRIS: 3.00 (95% CI 2.70–3.34; p <1e-04).

Open-access bias. Records whose DOI is missing from CRIS have an OA share of 76.6% versus 57.3% for matched records (difference +19.3 pp; chi-squared p <1e-04, statistically significant). Using all OpenAlex-UOC records instead of CRIS-confirmed ones shifts the institutional OA rate by +8.7 pp.

Interpretation. The institutional OA rate is overestimated when all OpenAlex-UOC records are used instead of CRIS-confirmed ones. Among OA records whose DOI is not in CRIS, the identified causes are: 1. Erroneous UOC affiliation (ORCID not in CRIS) 24.6%; 2. Dataset / other typology (outside CRIS scope) 29.3%; 3. Non-academic opinion / outreach journal 17.3%; Unexplained (to be investigated) 28.7%.

7 Metadata consistency on shared DOIs

Do records matched by DOI carry the same metadata in both systems? The analysis covers 5,881 DOIs present in both (one record per DOI per system).

7.1 Scorecard

Agreement between CRIS and OpenAlex metadata
Field Pairs compared Pairs in agreement Agreement
Document type 5,881 5,363 91.2%
Publication year (exact) 5,881 4,841 82.3%
Publication year (±1 year) 5,881 5,743 97.7%
Open-access status 5,881 4,598 78.2%
Language 5,828 5,505 94.5%

7.2 Document type

Reading. Document type agrees in 91.2% of pairs. The most frequent mismatches are CRIS Review → OpenAlex Article (27.2% of mismatches); CRIS Book Chapter → OpenAlex Conference Paper (9.1% of mismatches); CRIS Editorial → OpenAlex Article (8.1% of mismatches).

7.3 Publication year

Reading. Publication year agrees within ±1 year in 97.7% of pairs (exact: 82.3%). Among the 1,040 pairs whose year differs, 86.7% differ by exactly one year, and in 94.8% CRIS carries the later year (difference = CRIS − OpenAlex).

7.4 Open-access status

The two flags are not strictly equivalent: the CRIS flag reflects deposit/open availability as recorded by the institution, whereas OpenAlex is_oa reflects any open copy detected on the web (Unpaywall-based).

Open-access disagreements, taking CRIS as reference
Pairs compared False positives (OpenAlex OA, CRIS closed) % of OpenAlex OA records % of all pairs False negatives (OpenAlex closed, CRIS OA) % of OpenAlex closed records % of all pairs
5,881 437 13.0% 7.4% 846 33.6% 14.4%

Reading. OA status agrees in 78.2% of pairs. OpenAlex flags fewer records as OA than CRIS does (437 false positives vs. 846 false negatives). Rates: false positives 13% of OpenAlex OA records, false negatives 33.6% of OpenAlex closed records.

Reading. OpenAlex mean citations (23.3) are lower than Scopus (23.9), higher than Web of Science (21.4) and higher than Dimensions (22.1). Share of zero-cited documents: OpenAlex 17.3%, Scopus 10.5%, Web of Science 12.5%, Dimensions 17.3%. Spearman ρ with OpenAlex: Scopus 0.97, Web of Science 0.95, Dimensions 0.98.

7.6 Language

Reading. Language agrees in 94.5% of pairs.

8 Conclusions and next steps

Conclusions

  • Coverage. 26.1% of OpenAlex DOIs missing from CRIS are explained by erroneous UOC affiliations (72.4% of them are Article; 75.4% were published in 2018 or later (median year 2021)); datasets/“Other” types (1,547 records (27.4% of missing DOIs): Dataset (979), Other (568); main sources: Harvard Dataverse (871), Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research) (101), SSRN Electronic Journal (88)) and outreach journals (747 records (13.2% of missing DOIs): COMeIN (547), Mosaic (200)) explain a further share. Of the CRIS DOIs not matched to UOC works, 87.9% exist in OpenAlex without UOC affiliation and 12.1% are absent. Among the 401 absent records, the main typology is Dataset (67.3%) and the main editor/publisher is Repositori de dades de recerca (36.4%).
  • Open-access bias. Records whose DOI is missing from CRIS have an OA share of 76.6% versus 57.3% for matched records (difference +19.3 pp; chi-squared p <1e-04, statistically significant). Using all OpenAlex-UOC records instead of CRIS-confirmed ones shifts the institutional OA rate by +8.7 pp. The institutional OA rate is overestimated with all OpenAlex-UOC records. Among OA records whose DOI is not in CRIS, the identified causes are: 1. Erroneous UOC affiliation (ORCID not in CRIS) 24.6%; 2. Dataset / other typology (outside CRIS scope) 29.3%; 3. Non-academic opinion / outreach journal 17.3%; Unexplained (to be investigated) 28.7%.
  • Metadata. Across 5,881 shared DOIs: document type agrees in 91.2% of cases, publication year in 82.3% (exact), and open-access status in 78.2%. Among the 1,040 pairs whose year differs, 86.7% differ by exactly one year, and in 94.8% CRIS carries the later year (difference = CRIS − OpenAlex). The most frequent mismatches are CRIS Review → OpenAlex Article (27.2% of mismatches); CRIS Book Chapter → OpenAlex Conference Paper (9.1% of mismatches); CRIS Editorial → OpenAlex Article (8.1% of mismatches).
  • Open-access flag errors (CRIS as reference). OpenAlex reports OA where CRIS says closed in 13.0% of its OA records (false positives) and closed where CRIS says OA in 33.6% of its closed records (false negatives). OpenAlex flags fewer records as OA than CRIS does (437 false positives vs. 846 false negatives).
  • Citations. OpenAlex mean citations (23.3) are lower than Scopus (23.9), higher than Web of Science (21.4) and higher than Dimensions (22.1). Share of zero-cited documents: OpenAlex 17.3%, Scopus 10.5%, Web of Science 12.5%, Dimensions 17.3%. Spearman ρ with OpenAlex: Scopus 0.97, Web of Science 0.95, Dimensions 0.98.
